I'm 62, been farming these 12 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. It's just me and my old man at home now — our son works in Shijiazhuang and only comes back if he can get leave. So I have to plan around what two old people can actually manage. Cotton pays better but the picking kills your back, so I keep 5 mu in cotton, same as last year. That's about all we can pick ourselves. The other 7 mu I put in winter wheat last fall, and I'll plant maize right after we cut the wheat in June. Cotton is my main system, but I need the grain too.

The wheat is up and greening. It's April now, time to topdress. I usually spread about 15 kg of urea per mu before the wheat joints, then run the pump to wash it in. Pumping isn't cheap — electricity runs about 30 yuan per mu each time — so I'll water the wheat twice more: now with the fertilizer, and once more at heading in May if the rain doesn't come. I put down compound fertilizer at planting last fall, so all told the wheat gets about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu. Last year we got 420 kg per mu, but I'm only counting on 400. Better to be surprised on the upside.

For cotton, I'll plant around April 22nd. I buy hybrid seed from the supply shop in town — 60 yuan per mu, which stings, but the old local seed just doesn't compare. I plow and ridge the field first, then put down compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 30 kg per mu. When the cotton flowers in July, I'll topdress with another 10 kg of urea per mu and maybe some potassium. Cotton needs water at flowering and when the bolls are filling, so two irrigations. The real money goes to pesticide — aphids show up every year, and if the bollworm comes I have to spray two or three times. That's 80 to 100 yuan per mu just for chemicals. I hope for 250 kg per mu of seed cotton.

Maize goes in the ground June 10th or so, right after the combine finishes the wheat. We hire the combine — 50 yuan per mu — because at our age cutting 7 mu by hand would take forever and we'd miss the planting window. I plant Zhengdan 958 like everyone else, 40 yuan per mu for seed. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and then urea at the big trumpet stage, about 16 kg of nitrogen total per mu. Maize usually needs one good irrigation at tasseling, maybe another if August turns dry. Two times total. I spray herbicide once and keep an eye out for corn borer. Last year was good, 480 kg per mu, but I'll expect 450 kg.

Money is the hard part. I've got about 4,000 yuan put aside for this season's inputs. Cotton eats the most because of the seed and pesticide, so I thought about cutting back on wheat fertilizer, but that's false economy — if the wheat fails, I lose more than I save. I trimmed the maize seed cost by not buying the most expensive bag, and I'll do the spraying myself instead of hiring the crop duster. All together I need about 4,200 yuan, so I'll be a little short and might need to borrow 200 from my sister. That's farming.
